q: 1. The datum temperature for maturity by plowman is
explain: Plowman's maturity concept uses a datum temperature of −11.7°C (i.e., 11.7°C below zero), below which concrete strength gain is taken as effectively zero.

q: 2. ISI has specified the full strength of concrete after
explain: As per Indian Standards Institution (ISI/BIS) practice, the full/characteristic strength of concrete is specified and evaluated at 28 days of curing.

q: 3. For compacting plain concrete road surface of thickness less than 20 cm, we use
explain: For thin road slabs (less than 20 cm thick), a screed vibrator (surface vibrator) that runs along the screed board is used for effective compaction.

q: 4. When the concrete mix is too wet, it caused
explain: A too-wet concrete mix leads to segregation of aggregates, reduces density after settlement, and produces excess laitance (weak cement-water layer) at the surface, all occurring together.

q: 5. For compacting large sections of mass concrete in structures, the types of vibrator used is
explain: Internal (needle) vibrators are inserted directly into the concrete mass and are best suited for compacting large sections of mass concrete.

q: 6. Steam curing is not recommended for the concrete using
explain: High alumina cement is highly sensitive to elevated curing temperatures, which can cause conversion reactions that seriously reduce its strength, so steam curing is not recommended for it.

q: 7. Curing period required is minimum for the concrete using
explain: Rapid hardening cement gains strength very quickly, so the minimum curing period required for concrete made with it is the shortest among the options.

q: 8. High temperature
options: has no effect on the strength of concrete
explain: Elevated curing or ambient temperatures generally lead to reduced ultimate strength of concrete due to faster but less uniform hydration and increased porosity.

q: 9. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: The concrete gains strength due to hydration of cement
The concrete cured at a temperature below 23°C, gains strength up to 28 days
The concrete does not set at freezing point
The strength of concrete increases with its age
explain: All four statements are correct: hydration drives strength gain, curing temperature and duration affect the rate of gain, hydration effectively stops at freezing point, and strength continues to increase with the age of the concrete.

q: 10. At freezing point of water, concrete
explain: At the freezing point, water needed for the hydration reaction turns to ice and is unavailable to react chemically with cement, so hydration (setting) effectively stops.

q: 11. The approximate ratio of strength of cement concrete at 3 months to that of 28 days of curing
explain: Concrete continues to gain strength beyond 28 days as hydration progresses further; empirically, the strength at 3 months is roughly 1.15 times the 28-day strength.

q: 12. Proper batching ensures
explain: Accurate batching of ingredients in the correct proportions ensures the concrete achieves economy, workability, and the intended strength simultaneously.

q: 13. Strength of concrete with passage of time
explain: As hydration continues over time, the strength of concrete continues to increase, particularly noticeable in the months following the standard 28-day test.

q: 14. The breaking up and remixing of concrete that has layers to set is called
explain: Resetting is the process of breaking up concrete that has already begun to set in layers and remixing it, typically done when placement is delayed beyond the initial setting time.

q: 15. Which type of vibrator is generally used in concrete work?
explain: The needle (internal) vibrator is the most commonly used type in general concrete work, as it can be inserted directly into the concrete mass for thorough compaction.

q: 16. An ideal ware house, is provided
options: 15cm thick concrete floor laid on a dry course of soling
explain: An ideal cement warehouse must have all these features together - waterproof walls and roof, few closed windows, and a proper concrete floor on dry soling - to protect stored cement from moisture.

q: 17. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: space between the exterior walls of a ware house and bag piles should be 30 cm
cement bags should preferably be piled on wooden planks
cement bags should be placed such that bags of one layer does not touch the bags of the adjacent layer
width and height of the pile should not exceed 3 m and 2.70 m respectively
explain: All four statements (a-d) describe correct, standard warehouse storage practices for cement bags, so 'none of the above' (i.e., all are correct) is the right answer.

q: 18. The internal dimensions of a ware house are 15m x 5.6m, and the maximum height of piles is 2.70 m. The maximum number of bags to be stored in two piles, are
explain: Based on the given warehouse dimensions (15m x 5.6m) with a maximum stacking height of 2.70 m, divided into two piles, the calculated maximum storage capacity works out to 3000 bags.

q: 19. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: with passage of time, the strength of cement increases
with passage of time, the strength of cement decreases
after a period of 24 months, the strength of cement reduces to 50 %
The concrete made with storage deteriorated cement, gains strength with time
explain: Cement strength actually decreases (not increases) over prolonged storage time due to gradual absorption of atmospheric moisture and partial hydration, making statement (a) incorrect.

q: 20. Quality control means
options: a rational use of available resources
explain: Quality control fundamentally refers to the rational and efficient use of available resources (materials, labour, equipment) to consistently achieve the desired quality standards.

q: 21. The process of keeping concrete moist for a certain period after its finishing, is known as
explain: Curing is defined as the process of maintaining adequate moisture in concrete for a specified period after finishing, to ensure proper hydration and strength gain.

q: 22. Proper batching ensures
explain: Accurate batching of concrete ingredients ensures all these desirable qualities together - economical use of materials, durability, workability, and required strength of the finished concrete.

q: 23. The process of mixing some mortar in the mixer at the beginning of the first batch concrete mixing is called
explain: 'Buttering' refers to the practice of first mixing a small quantity of mortar in the drum before the main batch, to coat the mixer surfaces and prevent loss of cement paste from the first actual batch.

q: 24. During manufacture of concrete minimum period for which mixing is done in mixer for manufactured/crushed aggregate is (IS 456:2000)
explain: As per IS 456:2000, for concrete made with manufactured (crushed) aggregate, the minimum mixing period specified in the mixer is 2 minutes, since crushed aggregates require more thorough mixing.

q: 25. The concrete mixers are normally classified on the basis of
options: the technique of discharging the mixed concrete
explain: Concrete mixers are classified based on multiple criteria simultaneously - their discharge mechanism, batch capacity, and number of drums.

q: 26. The concrete can be lifted by pumps through a maximum vertical distance of
explain: As per the pump capability referenced in this text, concrete can typically be lifted vertically through a maximum distance of about 50 m.

q: 27. The diameter of pipeline used for transportation of concrete by pumps should not exceed
explain: As given in this text, the pipeline diameter used for pumping concrete should not exceed about 30 cm.

q: 28. Vertical sides of column may be stripped after
explain: Since vertical column sides are non-load-bearing formwork, they can be stripped relatively early, typically within 1 to 2 days.

q: 29. Surface vibrator is effective only when the thickness of concrete member does not exceed
explain: Surface vibrators are effective only for compacting relatively thin concrete sections, with their effectiveness limited to a thickness not exceeding 200 mm.

q: 30. Steam curing is used in
explain: Steam curing is primarily employed in the mass production of precast concrete elements, where accelerated strength gain is needed to allow rapid mould turnover in factory settings.

q: 31. Curing period is minimum for concrete using
explain: High alumina cement gains strength extremely rapidly (within 24 hours it can achieve strength comparable to 28-day OPC concrete), so it requires the minimum curing period among the given cement types.

q: 32. The main object of compaction of concrete is
options: to provide intimate contact between the concrete and embedded materials
explain: Compaction removes entrapped air, densifies the mix, and ensures concrete is in intimate contact with reinforcement/embedded parts — all these are objectives of compaction.

q: 33. What is the process of smoothening the surface of newly placed concrete with a trowel called?
explain: The operation of smoothening and levelling the surface of freshly placed concrete is termed floating, carried out with a float/trowel before final finishing.
